recipes.name: Jalapeno Popper Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 8 mushrooms, stems removed and chopped and caps reserved
1 jalapeno pepper, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped

steps.text: Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Crumble bacon; set aside.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a baking dish with cooking spray.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add chopped mushroom stems, jalapeño, and garlic; cook and stir until mushrooms release moisture and soften, about 10 minutes. Transfer to a bowl; stir in cream cheese, Cheddar cheese, and bacon. Season with salt and black pepper. Spoon cheese mixture generously into mushroom caps; place in the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese begins to brown, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeno Popper Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: These bite-sized appetizers are creamy, spicy, and cheesy. Why choose between stuffed mushrooms or jalapeno poppers when you can have both? At the same time!

video.description: So easy to make, these quick cheesy appetizers pack a bit of bite in every bite of their savory deliciousness! Cook chopped mushroom stems with garlic and jalapeno until softened, then combine with cream cheese, Cheddar cheese and crumbled bacon. Spoon generous portions into mushroom caps, then bake until cheese is browned and you can wait no longer!

review.reviewBody: Super yummy!! One thing I found is if you bake the mushrooms for a few minutes first, set them on paper towel to drain. Then when you bake them with the filling, the mushrooms will not get soggy.

So delicious! But since it's kind of a pain to make a lot of them for parties, this time I'm trying it as a dip - 8 slices of bacon, two very large jalapenos, a 5-oz. container of sliced mushrooms that I dices, 2 8-oz. packages of cream cheese, and half a cup of cheese. Make as usual, but spread into an 8"x8" pan and sprinkled a little extra cheese on top, baked for 10-15 minutes. Much easier to make a crowd pleaser that way!

oooooo so yummy! I used the package jalapeno bacon bits, I also added crab meat and extra cheese, and cayenne pepper. I mixed it with my blender. After doubling the recipe, I had a little extra filling, so I used the rest for jalapenos. yummmmy!

Very tasty! I made a couple of changes: Used Costco bacon bits instead of making my own, and as per other suggestions, pre-baked the mushrooms for 20 minutes (after removing the stems for the filling) and drained them before stuffing them, and also added a couple of shakes of cayenne pepper to the filling. Deelish and a definite party favorite; will make these again!

Very tasty! I made a couple of changes: Used Costco bacon bits instead of making my own, and as per other suggestions, pre-baked the mushrooms for 20 minutes (after removing the stems for the filling) and drained them before stuffing them, and also added a couple of shakes of cayenne pepper to the filling. Deelish and a definite party favorite; will make these again!

Great recipe. I baked them on a wire rack over a cookie sheet so they wouldn't get soggy, and so the bottom of the mushrooms will get the benefit of dry heat. I also put the stuffing in a sandwich bag, clipped off a corner, and squeezed the stuffing into the mushrooms (much easier and less messy). Next time I'm definitely leaving the ribs in, maybe even add another jalapeno or two. And I would add lemon juice to the stuffing - it needed acid imho. But they're also fantastic just the way they are.

These were soooo good! I had a large package of baby bellas so I tripled the ingredients. I baked the mushrooms for a few minutes before stuffing to reduce the liquid. I also broiled them for a minute or so after stuffing and baking to toast them a little on top. My husband loved them! He likes spicy so I used four jalepenos with seeds which gave them a lot of heat. They are low carb too so works with our diet. I'm sure these will become a regular at our house. Thanks for the recipe!!

Amazing! I used 6 large white mushrooms and cooked the mushrooms stems, garlic, and jalapeno in the bacon fat instead of olive oil. I will make this again and again. I love that it is low carb too! Thanks for a winning recipe, CookinBug!

These were easy to make and taste great. I did make one addition to give more of the popper quality to them. I rolled 1/2 of them in garlic & herb seasoned bread crumbs before baking to give them a little crunch.. just the cream cheese not the mushroom... but I might try all of the mushrooom next time. The ones with bread crumbs definitely were better. MIght try panko as well next time for even more crunch. Definitely will be a repeat!

Oh my goodness, these were SO good!! I used some of the bacon fat to sautee the mushroom stems, garlic etc, instead of olive oil. Really helped round out the flavour. Also used jalapeno slices in a jar, as I had none fresh. I followed another reviewer's suggestion and pre-baked the mushrooms stem side down in the oven for 5-10 minutes and then drained them on paper towels to get the excess moisture out, before filling. This helped quite a bit to maintain a wonderful texture to the mushrooms without them getting mushy. Make these.....NOW!!!

Yum! I baked them for about 10 min before filling to drain the water out of them. I used diced summer sausage instead of bacon just for the ease of it. That was very good, but I'm sure the bacon is good too. Topped with panko bread crumbs.
Delicious! Next time, more bacon.
Following the recipe as is and these turned out good.
quick easy and wonderfully delicious!
We have to double the number of mushrooms because there is too much filling.

Used Baby Bella mushrooms and a small cookie scoop to fill the mushroom caps. A couple things that I will add next time are some seasoned salt and more cheddar. We thoroughly enjoyed these as an appetizer.
Make this all the time my family absolutely loves it I always have to double the recipe. Only thing I do differently is I roast the jalapeños and take skin off

Made for our appetizer-themed Christmas and, since there were a couple vegetarian guests - omitted the bacon. I know you may ask how is that a jalapeño popper mushroom without the bacon?? Well, my solution was that I had some bacon flavored salt. While I tend to subscribe to the “bacon makes everything better” these were great without! And devoured! Will make again! With or without the bacon! Thanks CookinBug!
Made these for a Christmas party and they went like hotcakes! I doubled the recipe and used smaller mushrooms so each would be 1-2 bites, and it made more to go around. Everyone loved them!
Delicious! I used large portobello mushroom caps and added bread crumbs to the filling. Hubby loved it!
